title: Claims/assets 1974 archival follow-up: substantive records and access audit

sources.title: Memorandum of conversation: Secretary Kissinger’s Visit to Peking, Counterpart Discussions on Exchanges and Claims/Assets (First Session), November 26, 1974
sources.source_type: Contemporaneous US State Department meeting record preserved as an official archival scan

reading_scope.read: Physical 40–49 of the 50-page scan: complete ten-page first-session record, printed 1–10. Folder cover/index (physical 1–3) and final continuation notice also inspected. Other meeting records not systematically read.
reading_scope.visual_checks: Physical 40, 46–48: header, printed 7–9; checked speaker attribution where OCR separates labels.

findings.finding: Habib treated the $17 million offer as accepted, described governmental noninvolvement in old bonds, and tied asset identification to US law and litigation protection. He asked whether an agreement in principle remained.

Lin identified the June 14, 1974 reply as answering the December 22, 1973 US memorandum. He objected to designated-national language and old liabilities; Habib denied requiring Chinese acknowledgment of old liabilities and offered flexibility in wording.

Lin explained the offer as conditional on an understanding about settlement of old liabilities; he said the December response did not conform to the November commitment and linked that alleged failure to withdrawal. Habib disputed the difference and undertook to examine it again. No settlement reached in this session.

limits: American record of attributed Chinese and American positions, not Chinese minutes or instructions.

The June 14 reply, December 22 US memorandum, and underlying succession of drafts were not recovered. This record cannot decide whether an assurance was broken or whether the attributed explanation exhausted internal reasons.
Lin’s statement and Habib’s disagreement must both be preserved. A technical characterization is Habib’s position, not a neutral determination of the remaining legal stakes.
sources.archive: Gerald R. Ford Presidential Library, Kissinger Reports on USSR, China, and Middle East Discussions, Box 2, November 25–29, 1974—Kissinger’s Trip (1)
sources.source_independence: A contemporary American official record; do not count its later use by Solomon as independent corroboration of the same exchange.

sources.title: Memorandum of conversation: Secretary Kissinger’s Visit to Peking, Counterpart Talks—Claims and Exchanges, October 22, 1975
sources.source_type: Contemporaneous US State Department meeting record preserved as an official archival scan

reading_scope.depth: Selected sections; complete claims exchanges and immediate context
reading_scope.read: Physical 4–8 / printed 1–5 (header, opening, complete US claims proposal); physical 13–14 / printed 10–11 (transition and complete Lin response); physical 19–20 / printed 16–17 (complete closing). Meeting occupies physical 4–20 within 38-page folder. Intervening cultural-exchange passages and later documents not completely read.
reading_scope.visual_checks: Physical 4, 7, 8, 14: header and printed 4, 5, 11. Physical 2, 3, 21 inspected as image-only folder dividers, not missing draft texts.

findings.finding: Habib proposed withdrawing the March 21, 1973 US statement and October 27, 1973 aide-mémoire on bonds; offered matching asset-identification wording in the main agreement or an exchange of letters; sought restoration of Zhou’s repayment offer within the package.

Lin explicitly said the June 14, 1974 letter withdrew the monetary offer regarding assets already recovered from third-country banks. He maintained the bond position and rejected proposed definitions as imposition of US law on Chinese affairs.
Habib ended further claims discussion at that meeting, but still asked at the close that both sides study the ideas. This is not evidence that all subsequent contact ended.

limits: The proposed withdrawal is not proof that the statements were actually rescinded.
The paper handed over is described but exact underlined language is not supplied in the read passages. No legal equivalence of the alternatives established.
No Chinese internal authorization recovered. Solomon attended this meeting: his later account is not another independent witness.

sources.title: Memorandum of conversation, Washington, April 29, 1977: Claims/assets; FRUS 1977–1980, Volume XIII, document 27
sources.source_type: Official edited publication of a contemporaneous US memorandum

reading_scope.read: Complete published body and all four editorial notes. Official HTML, not original archival scan. Previously identified and read as a lead in the Chapter 1 developmental work; reacquired here.

findings.locator: Han Hsu’s opening statement and discussion
findings.finding: Han stated three objections and asserted continuity with the November 1973 and June 14, 1974 positions. This is an attributed negotiating claim, not proof of the missing message’s complete wording.

Identifies telegram 985 from Beijing, June 14, 1974, National Archives, RG 59, Central Foreign Policy File, no film number. The note’s term “agreement” must not be taken to establish a bilateral agreement contrary to the contested primary descriptions.

limits: This is an archival locator and later attributed statement, not the June 14 original.
Do not count as a newly discovered meeting: the prior development memo already identified the entry.

interpretation_limits: Two later contemporary US records materially strengthen process reconstruction but are not recovery of the missing Chinese instrument.
Lin’s stated conditionality and Habib’s denial are competing positions. Neither alone establishes a broken commitment or excludes internal political causes.
Finding aids are separated from historical evidence; access failures do not establish archival absence or classification.
No outreach, purchase, account creation or chapter/shared-apparatus edit performed.
